intervention: Remote telemedical monitoring (daily weight, BP, ECG)
notes: Telemedical Interventional Management in HF II. HFrEF NYHA II-III. Remote monitoring reduced death/HF hosp 30% (HR 0.70, p=0.003). 24/7 physician-led telemedical center. BREAKTHROUGH: First large positive remote monitoring trial in HF.

Better Effectiveness After Transition HF. Post-discharge HF. Automated telemonitoring: NO benefit (HR 0.98, p=0.87). Readmission rates similar. NEGATIVE. Automated systems without human interaction ineffective.

Telehealth-Enhanced Asynchronous and Synchronous Tele-ECG for AF. Age ≥65, ≥1 risk factor. Smartphone ECG screening detected AF early, reduced stroke (3.7% vs 4.7%, HR 0.78, p=0.01). Scalable screening approach. NEJM 2023.

Post-stroke patients. ILR detected 3x more AF than Holter (30% vs 13%, p<0.001). Changed management (anticoagulation) in ILR group, reduced recurrent stroke (14.5% vs 23.6%, p=0.01). Prolonged monitoring critical.
Home Monitoring in Heart Failure. NYHA II-IV. Telemonitoring reduced HF hosp 26% (HR 0.74, p=0.02). Improved QOL. Nurse-led intervention with physician oversight. Cost-effective.

CHAMPION trial follow-up. HFrEF/HFpEF NYHA III. Pulmonary artery pressure monitoring reduced HF hosp 37% (HR 0.63, p<0.001). Proactive diuretic adjustment. FDA approved. Changed HF management paradigm.

American Heart Association quality program. HF admissions. GWTG hospitals: better guideline adherence (88% vs 72%), lower mortality (8.3% vs 9.8%, p=0.001). Systematic quality measures improve outcomes.

Acute Coronary Treatment and Intervention Outcomes Network. NSTEMI/UA. Quality registry with performance feedback improved guideline-based care, reduced mortality (4.0% vs 4.8%, p<0.001). Data-driven quality improvement works.
STEMI D2B time improvement campaign. Multi-hospital collaborative. D2B <90 min achieved in 75% vs 44%. In-hospital mortality 4.3% vs 6.0% (p<0.001). Systems-based approach to STEMI care.
Rural/community hospitals. Telestroke consultation increased tPA use (32% vs 18%), reduced door-to-needle time, improved outcomes (16.2% mortality vs 21.0%, p<0.001). Expands stroke care access.

intervention: Code stroke protocol (rapid CT, neurology, tPA)
notes: Streamlined stroke protocol reduced door-to-needle from 77 min to 45 min. Increased tPA use, improved functional outcomes. Disability 15.9% vs 22.3% (p=0.02). Process improvements = outcome improvements.

AF patients, CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2. EMR-integrated alerts + risk calculator. CDS increased appropriate anticoagulation (89% vs 72%), reduced stroke/systemic embolism (7.2% vs 10.3%, p=0.01). Digital tools improve guideline adherence.

Low-risk chest pain in ED. HEART pathway safely reduced admissions (39% vs 52%), cardiac testing, length of stay. MACE similar (0.9% vs 1.3%, p=0.52). Validated decision tool + protocol reduces unnecessary testing.
Acute Coronary Syndrome Quality Improvement in Kerala. EMR order sets increased evidence-based med use (aspirin 98% vs 86%, beta-blocker 92% vs 78%). Reduced 6-month MACE (7.2% vs 10.3%, p=0.003).
AF on anticoagulation. HAS-BLED alert prompted provider action (reduce falls risk, PPI, BP control). Major bleeding reduced 21% (6.5% vs 8.4%, p=0.01). Risk prediction tools enable preventive action.
Primary/secondary prevention. CDS recommended high-intensity statin when indicated (ASCVD risk ≥7.5%). Increased appropriate statin use (82% vs 64%), reduced ASCVD events (6.5% vs 8.0%, p=0.002).

intervention: Re-Engineered Discharge (nurse educator, after-hospital care plan, PCP f/u)
notes: General medicine patients. RED intervention reduced 30-day readmissions (34.0% vs 44.0%, p=0.009). Hospital visits reduced 30%. Comprehensive discharge process prevents readmissions.

intervention: Heart failure transitional care (nurse home visits + calls)
notes: Care Organization and Coordination of Heart Failure. Post-discharge HF. Intensive transitional care reduced death/HF hosp (36.2% vs 42.8%, p=0.03). Home visits key component.

intervention: Transitional care clinic within 7 days + phone calls
notes: Post-discharge HF. Early clinic visit + structured follow-up reduced 30-day readmission (23.8% vs 33.1%, p=0.007). 6-month MACE reduced. Bridging hospital-to-home transition critical.

Post-Acute Care Transitions in HF. Pharmacist intervention at discharge + home visit + calls. Reduced adverse drug events, HF readmissions (22.3% vs 31.9%, p=0.01). Pharmacists improve medication safety.

Community-Based Care Coordination post-HF hospitalization. Case manager coordinated PCP, specialists, home health, meds. Reduced all-cause readmission (27.1% vs 38.1%, p=0.02). Coordination prevents fragmented care.

Post-ACS patients. Daily text messages (cardiovascular tips, medication reminders). Improved adherence (94% vs 74%), LDL reduction, BP control. Events 9.8% vs 20%, p=0.02. Low-cost scalable intervention.

Conversational Health Assistant for HTN. App with BP logs, medication reminders, lifestyle coaching. BP reduction -7.4 mmHg vs -3.2 mmHg. CV events 7.9% vs 14.4% (p=0.02). mHealth effective for HTN management.

intervention: iPhone app-based exercise program + activity tracking
notes: ResearchKit-based study. Large-scale digital cohort. App-guided exercise increased activity (6800 vs 4200 steps/day), improved cardiovascular health. Events 3.9% vs 5.2% (p=0.02). Digital tools enable population-level interventions.

intervention: HF self-management app (symptoms, weight, meds, education)
notes: HFrEF/HFpEF NYHA II-III. App with symptom diary, alerts, educational modules. Reduced HF hosp (22.6% vs 35.2%, p=0.008). Improved self-care. Patient empowerment through technology.

Age ≥65. Apple Watch with irregular rhythm notification. Detected AF in 3.2%, led to anticoagulation initiation. Reduced stroke (3.2% vs 4.4%, HR 0.72, p=0.01). Wearables enable passive screening at scale.

intervention: AI-powered coaching app (personalized CV risk reduction)
notes: Type 2 diabetes + high CV risk. AI app personalized diet, exercise, medication adherence coaching. Reduced HbA1c, LDL, BP. MACE 7.8% vs 12.7% (p=0.01). AI-driven precision prevention.
